## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Udakadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 499) is a canonical verse text situated within the Therāpadāna collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It records the narrative verse account associated with the elder Udakadāyaka. SuttaCentral records five translations of the text across five modern languages, but no curated external parallels [SuttaCentral].
Textual reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language matches in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora meeting the match threshold [DharmaNexus]. However, it reveals substantial internal reuse within the Pali canon, recording 111 matching passages across 53 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. These correspondences largely comprise standard formulaic verse sequences shared with other monastic life-story poems in the Apadāna. Notably, verses across segments §3.1–7.1 and §3.2–8.1 share high-similarity textual formulas with texts such as the *Ekāsanadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 425), *Gandhamuṭṭhiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 378), *Ajeliphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 509), *Yāgudāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 420), *Upaḍḍhadussadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 497), and the *Udakadāyikātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 10) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
